title: Dual-Model LLM Ensemble via Web Chat Interfaces Reaches Near-Perfect Sensitivity for Systematic-Review Screening: A Multi-Domain Validation with Equivalence to API Access

live_model.evidence: 'OpenAI's GPT-5 Thinking (gpt-5-2025-08-07) has an October 2024 knowledge cutoff...we configured API settings...OpenAI: reasoning effort = medium'; results: 'GPT-5 R1 API 288 42 264 142 87.3% (83.2%, 90.7%) 65.0% (60.2%, 69.7%)'

prompt.location: Methods ('Prompting and Screening Workflow'): zero-shot system prompt instructing PICOS-based screening, include/exclude/full-text-review classification, single-sentence justification, markdown-table output; batch sizes per review in Table 1
prompt.note: Prompt content and structure are thoroughly described (and PICOS criteria per review given), but the literal system-prompt text is not quoted verbatim.

claim.metric: sensitivity (%) vs. Cochrane human reference standard, GPT-5 Thinking via API, Run 1
claim.location: Results table, row 'GPT-5 R1 API' (288/42/264/142 confusion counts, summing to 736; specificity 65.0% in the same row)

data.source: 16 Cochrane Library systematic reviews (Issue 6, May-June 2025), 736 titles/abstracts with published inclusion/exclusion decisions

notes: The study deliberately runs a matched API condition alongside the GUI condition (2 models x 2 runs x 2 modalities), so the API numbers used here are not blocked by webui. A duplicate API run (R2) gives nearly identical results (87.9% sensitivity), and the GUI condition is separately reported for comparison.
